review_method: Project owner watched the clip and listed the ball sequence with timestamps, then separately described how Pipelines A, B and C each labelled the SAME sequence. The three pipelines disagree only on track ids, not on what happened, so the event sequence is the reference and ids are treated as run-specific.
scope: Complete annotation of 0-30s for this clip. One clip, one annotator, timestamps read to the nearest second, hence the 1.5s tolerance.
time_basis: clip seconds; pass time = RECEPTION, matching what the contact engine emits; a keeper kick is timed at the kick

id_spaces.note: Same ten real events under three runs. Useful for checking identity, useless as event labels.
id_spaces.pipeline_A: TA10 -> TA2 -> TA keeper 209 (kick) -> TB9 touch -> TA12 touch -> TB9 -> TB keeper 846 -> TB6 -> TB537 -> intercepted by TA1 -> TB5
id_spaces.pipeline_B: TA25 -> TA6 -> TA keeper 171 (kick) -> TB8 touch -> TA11 touch -> TB8 -> TB keeper 442 -> TB5 -> (TB player shown as TA16) -> TA12 -> TB2
id_spaces.known_defect: In B and C the receiver at ~26s is a TB player but is coloured TA16. That is the confirmed #3<->#16 team/ID error, not a different sequence.

notes: Five of these ten events send the ball INTO THE AIR (t=11 keeper kick, t=14 knee-high touch, t=16 kick to air, t=22 keeper kick, t=27 kick to air). contacts_v2 disables aerial contacts by design, so this clip is much harder for it than Messi, where only one pass was aerial.
t=24 is the reception of the keeper kick launched at t=22, annotated once at the reception.
t=28 is the interception of the ball kicked at t=27, annotated once at the interception.
Balls are received at the feet, so reception is judged at the foot position.
